solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 4 cut by ring on sailor's hand

indicators.note: the word for 4 is sliced open so that other letters sit inside it

parts.note: the clue number points to 4 down, whose solution means one who lures, a lurer

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, places the ring after the sailor, so it is written second

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue, a ring and a sailor's hand: a nautical jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' sends you to 4 down; its synonym LURER is what gets 'cut by' ABO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand or deckhand.

clue.text: Disease got from hair on rabbit

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
to rabbit is British slang for chattering, as is to jaw

explanation.surface: An infection caught from a rabbit's fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the animal; it is the British verb for talking endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is commonly called this because it stiffens the jaw muscles.

clue.text: Details not fleshed out?

parts.note: essentials only, like a skeleton with no flesh on it

explanation.surface: A query about information that has not been developed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means only the essential facts, with nothing extra, like a skeleton stripped of meat.

clue.text: Futile to economise?

definitions.meaning: futile means pointless, having no effect
to economise is to consume a smaller amount, split into two words

explanation.surface: Is cutting spending pointless?
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless serves no purpose, so it is of no use.

clue.text: Return key with one caught opening drawer

indicators.note: opening means these letters prise apart the key word and sit inside it

parts.note: the Return key on a keyboard is also labelled Enter
one is I in Roman numerals
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone presses Return and finds a drawer has sprung open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; it is one who draws people in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attracts or tempts others draws them in, so is a drawer.

clue.text: Move smoothly as rowing teams in sound

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word spoken that matches another, so the teams' word is said aloud

parts.note: the teams in rowing boats are crews

explanation.surface: Rowers glide across a stretch of sheltered water, a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a body of water for the rowers; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or ship that cruises travels at a steady, easy speed.

clue.text: Cruel remark makes fox and rat swap tails

indicators.note: swap tails says the two words exchange their final letters

parts.note: to fox someone is to trick them, to cheat
to rat is to inform on, to shop someone

explanation.surface: An insult is cooked up by exchanging the tails of two animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap tails' trades the last letters: CHEAT ends in P and SHOP ends in T.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfair, hurtful jibe aimed at a weak spot is a low blow.

clue.text: Impractical if fine vessel capsizes, blocking cross-channel one

indicators.note: blocking means these letters stand in the middle, between the others

parts.note: un is French for one, French being across the Channel

indicators.note: capsizes, in a down clue, says the boat is turned upside down so the letters run the other way

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 as I
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: A fine ship overturning in the Channel would be idealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic schemes for a perfect society are unrealistic and unworkable.

clue.text: Something in chest to check when entertaining wild run

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means taking them in, so this word holds the others

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it

indicators.note: wild means these letters run in a disordered order

explanation.surface: Checking a wild run on the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone in the middle of the ribcage.

clue.text: Inclined to punish vice with rector corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something spoilt and twisted out of shape, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A corrupt clergyman is disposed to punish wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrective measures are disciplinary, meant to put wrongdoers right by penalty.

clue.text: Baker, having finished, runs out at noon

indicators.note: out says the runs go missing from the word before

parts.note: when something is over it has finished
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A baker, his shift over, has run out of stock by midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like the tradesman; it is the thing that bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the appliance that bakes bread and cakes.

clue.text: Outline of duties for which patient may be employed?

definitions.meaning: a written summary of what a post involves

definitions.text: for which patient may be employed?
definitions.meaning: Job of the Bible is proverbially patient, so an account of him is the one patient's description

explanation.surface: A medical patient hired for a role, reading a summary of tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' seems to be someone under medical care; it is the patient one, Job of the Old Testament, famous for 'the patience of Job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A post's written specification lists its responsibilities for the holder.

clue.text: Earn an award, given by queen in royal residence

parts.note: to earn a prize is to win it
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military award
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Someone collects an honour from the monarch at a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: WINDSOR Castle is a residence of the British monarch west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle at that Berkshire town is one of the King's official homes.

clue.text: One's experienced men only in later years coming round

indicators.note: coming round says one word encircles the other

parts.note: in later years one is older
a stag party is for men only

explanation.surface: A man looks back on all-male gatherings as he ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran with long experience is a seasoned hand, an old-timer.

clue.text: Perhaps mobile, with its case, producing little sound

parts.note: a mobile is an example of a phone
the case of the word mobile is its outer letters, M and E

explanation.surface: A mobile in its protective case gives off a faint noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like the phone's cover; it means the outside letters of 'mobile'.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics a phoneme is a smallest unit of speech distinguishing one word from another.

clue.text: Russian fighter in East, respected, went from country

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
to be well rated is to be respected

explanation.surface: A Russian warplane in the East, highly regarded, left the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's homeland to settle abroad is to relocate overseas.

clue.text: Lawsuit involves rotter in dramatic fall

indicators.note: involves means the lawsuit word takes in the other inside it

parts.note: a lawsuit is a case in court
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A legal action against a scoundrel ends in a spectacular downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, water dropping steeply over rocks.

clue.text: Greed, for starters, and resulting in a wicked habit

indicators.note: in means those first letters are put inside the following words

parts.note: a vice is a wicked habit

indicators.note: for starters says take the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Greed, to begin with, leads to a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is a synonym, one of the seven deadly sins: excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Summer treat best to keep cold

indicators.note: to keep means the larger word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: the choice item is the best one
C is short for cold on taps

explanation.surface: The best summer treat should be kept cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British bar of ice cream coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen confections like chocolate-coated ice cream bars are hot-weather delights.

clue.text: Sit awkwardly with a man, revealing bottom

indicators.note: awkwardly says these letters are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sits awkwardly beside a man and flashes their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' looks anatomical; it is an old sense meaning staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom, in horse racing and boxing, means endurance or grit, the capacity to keep going.

clue.text: Poet is writer held by revolutionary communists

indicators.note: held by means the writer sits inside the other word
revolutionary hints at turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: communists are reds
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: A poet held captive by revolutionary communists.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was a 20th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet of the 1930s generation.

clue.text: Protein book now available at bookshop?

parts.note: an album is a book, as for photos or stamps
a book that is in is in stock

explanation.surface: A protein-themed book has just reached the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't confuse it with ALBUMEN, egg white.
explanation.definitionFit: This water-soluble protein is found in blood plasma and egg white.

clue.text: Blockhead is joining Eliot, perhaps, in seconds

parts.note: a blockhead is a fool, an ass
T.S. Eliot, the poet, has the initials TS

explanation.surface: A fool joins the poet Eliot in a matter of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like a unit of time; it is the verb 'to second', help.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to support or help them.

clue.text: As prosecutor be prepared for bribe

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A prosecutor ready to take a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder takes in the be of be prepared, so only prepared signals the anagram. In myth, Cerberus, the dog guarding Hades, was pacified with a drugged cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gift to placate an awkward person, as the guard dog of the underworld was placated.

clue.text: In Herculaneum I'm inside sewer, doomed

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A sewer under the Roman town buried by Vesuvius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain in ancient Herculaneum; it is someone who sews: the seamstress of Puccini's opera La bohème, who dies at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Puccini's opera is an embroiderer who dies of consumption.

clue.text: Irish writer succeeded in London college

parts.note: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish author of She Stoops to Conquer
S is short for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: An Irish author did well at a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a college of the University of London in New Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: This institution is part of London University, famed for art and design.

clue.text: Facing archdeacon, counterpart appearing powerless

parts.note: an archdeacon is titled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: powerless means the letter for power, P, is dropped from the word

parts.note: a peer is an equal, one's counterpart

explanation.surface: An archdeacon confronts an equal who appears to have lost influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A facing is a thin surface layer over cheaper material, as on furniture.

clue.text: Pomegranate syrup's missing in pineapples

indicators.note: missing means the word that follows is taken away

parts.note: grenadine is a pomegranate syrup; the 's gives the plural form

explanation.surface: Pomegranate syrup is absent from a pineapple dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pineapples' is old soldiers' slang for hand bombs, from their segmented shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang called hand bombs pineapples for their ridged casing.
